title: The Exiled Covenant Breakers
intro: In the early days of a fledgling community, a tribe once lived in fortified dwellings, bound by a pact. When that pact was betrayed, the consequences echoed through the pages of the Quran. Who were these people, and what became of their homes and orchards?
clues: We dwelt in strongholds that gave us a false sense of security.
We were people of the Scripture, yet we broke our covenant.
We plotted against the messenger after he came to us, but our scheme failed.
Our palm trees were cut down by the command of Allah, a sign of His power.
We were expelled from our homes, never to return, as a punishment for our defiance.
The Quran mentions us in the chapter of the gathering, and our story serves as a warning for those who break pacts.

trial.label: Trial/Event
options: Siege and expulsion from their homes
trial.answer: Siege and expulsion from their homes

arabic: مَا قَطَعْتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوهَا قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيُخْزِىَ ٱلْفَـٰسِقِينَ
verse: Whatever you have cut down of [their] palm trees or left standing on their trunks - it was by permission of Allāh and so He would disgrace the defiantly disobedient. (59:5)
